items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: it’s the same thing with Sam. He starts off and he structures us and guides us through

ctx.x: Because I just had the wonderful opportunity to hear “The Rite of Spring” performed live, and I was thinking after I left last night that that came to mind. Because some of the stuff you did almost reminded me of parts of that piece, and I could envision Stravinsky writing all that complex music. You guys achieved the same feel with three people being spontaneous.

Exactly. See that’s the thing. I mean that’s the thing about the whole new music, what they call the new music classical scene, you know. What happens is that for some strange reason, you know, like people like to divide people and put them in boxes and everything. No. If you go to a new music concert of ensemble concerts, you’ll probably hear a lot of the things that we played, most definitely, yeah. But you know so if you go to a new music ensemble concert you’ll hear a lot of the elements that we play on…

that they’re doing. Everything is just smooth and beautiful [scats]. And I mean it’s beautiful and technically proficient but sometimes you got to yell out and scream you know. You just can’t be talking in a conversational mode, even though it might be intellectually stimulating and beautiful and amazing technique and everything. Because sometimes you need to yell out and just go, “I need to scream.” And that’s what happens. You saw that with Scott. I mean Scott just, I mean you know how proficient and he can…
